text:
The president last hinted at running for a third term in May(Image: AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

President Donald Trump suggested running for a third term, announcing on Thursday that he plans to be "the next president."

President Trump, whose marriage to Melania is at its lowest point for one humiliating reason, has repeatedly expressed his desire to flout the 22nd Amendment, which bars U.S. presidents from serving more than two terms in office, during his second presidential term. He did so again on Thursday while touting America's progress in the artificial intelligence race against China at the Environmental Protection Agency headquarters in Washington, D.C.

"All I know is I'd like to be the next president, because I'm going to make somebody look very good," he said, appearing to enrage users online who rebuked a potential third Trump administration. It comes after Trump's assistant was told to 'change his diaper' in an awkward moment caught on camera.

"Does he know he's currently the president?" one joked.

"Dementia must be bad. He thinks he is in 2012," another wrote.

The 80-year-old president has not let up on this claim since reclaiming the White House in January 2025(Image: AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

"God no. No 3rd term," a third added.

The president last hinted at running for a third term in May while delivering the keynote address the U.S. Coast Guard Academy commencement ceremony. He eerily said he'd remain at the helm of the country for years to come.

"I'm gonna be here in '28. Maybe I'll be here in '32, too."

Expectedly, social media users rejected the notion, with one posting "Nah. Trump is a lame duck who's aging rapidly. In 2032 Trump will be 85; he already falls asleep and has health issues he's keeping secret. Besides: all the man really cares about is his ballroom. His will be the grandest of all!"

Trump loyalists within the judicial branch of government have refused to speak against the president(Image: Getty Images)

Another stated, "First president convicted of 34 felonies hints at staying until '32. The 22nd Amendment exists. Read it. "No he f------- won't," declared another frustrated user. "Patriotic Americans will make sure of that."

A third said: "The Constitution and his rapidly decomposing purple hands would disagree."

The 80-year-old president has not let up on this claim since reclaiming the White House in January 2025, leaving Americans on the edge of their seats as President Trump seeks to consolidate power and ignore decorum and laws he swore to protect at his inauguration.

The president suggested there are "methods which you could do it"(Image: AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

Moreover, Trump loyalists within the judicial branch of government have refused to go against the president, begging the question of whether they'd allow him to break the law.

Earlier this year in May, Trump-appointed Texas Judge John George Edward Marck refused to confirm whether the U.S. Constitution prohibits a commander-in-chief from serving a third term during his Senate Judiciary Committee confirmation hearing.

It's unclear how Trump would get away with going against the Constitution, but the president suggested there are "methods which you could do it," in August of last year without providing details.

"It is far too early to think about it," he added.

It comes after Trump sparked outrage as he announced his disgraceful new plan.
